title: Materials forming the crust of the earth
competency: Identify the major elements, minerals and rocks that form the crust.

keywords.def: The simplest substances. Eight elements, led by oxygen and silicon, make about 98% of the crust.
Natural non-living solids with a fixed structure and chemical make-up. The building blocks of rocks.
Rock formed when magma or lava cools and hardens. From the Latin ignis, fire.
Rock formed in layers from settled sediments. Holds fossils, coal, oil and gas.
Rock formed when heat and pressure change an existing rock. Example: marble.
Extrusive igneous rock that cooled on the surface, such as basalt.
Intrusive igneous rock that cooled deep inside the Earth, such as granite.
The change of existing rocks into new rocks by heat and pressure.
Molten rock below the Earth's surface.
Magma that has reached the Earth's surface.
A dark extrusive igneous rock formed from cooled lava.
The most common intrusive igneous rock, used as building stone.

en.text: The crust is made of many elements. About 98% of it is made of just eight. Oxygen is the most common at 46.6%. Silicon is next at 27.72%. Then come aluminium, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium and magnesium.

am.text: የመሬት ቅርፊት ከብዙ ንጥረ ነገሮች የተሠራ ነው። 98% ያህሉ ከስምንት ብቻ የተሠራ ነው። ኦክስጅን 46.6% ሆኖ በብዛት ቀዳሚ ነው። ሲሊከን 27.72% ሆኖ ይከተላል። ከዚያም አሉሚኒየም፣ ብረት፣ ካልሲየም፣ ሶዲየም፣ ፖታሲየምና ማግኒዚየም ይመጣሉ።

screens.title: What is under your feet?
screens.text: Pick up a stone from your school compound.
screens.ask: Which element do you think is most common in the Earth's crust?
screens.after: It is oxygen! It is locked inside the rocks. Check the table below.

screens.title: 1.4.1 Major elements
paras: The crust is made of many elements.
Near the surface they are solid. Deep inside they are hot and molten.
About 98% of the crust is made of just eight elements.
screens.note: Table 1.1 Most common elements in the Earth's crust, % by weight. Source: Fleischer, Data of Geochemistry (1967).

screens.title: Building materials of the crust
defs: Elements
The simplest substances. Eight elements, led by oxygen and silicon, make about 98% of the crust.

screens.title: The big two
screens.text: Which two elements make up about three quarters of the crust?
screens.clue: Look at the two biggest numbers in Table 1.1.

screens.title: Eight elements
screens.ask: About ___% of the crust is made of just eight elements.
screens.why: Oxygen, silicon, aluminium, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium and magnesium.
screens.clue: Read the first paragraph of 1.4.1 again.

screens.title: Iron in the crust
screens.text: Iron is the most common element in the Earth's crust.
screens.why: Iron is about 5%. Oxygen (46.6%) is the most common.
screens.clue: Find iron in Table 1.1. Is it at the top?

screens.title: Silicon in a rock
screens.text: A 100 kg rock has the same make-up as the average crust.
screens.ask: About ___ kg of it is silicon.
screens.why: Silicon is 27.72% by weight. 27.72% of 100 kg is 27.72 kg, about 28 kg.
screens.clue: Per cent means out of 100. Find silicon's percentage.
screens.worked: Silicon is 27.72% of the crust. 27.72% of 100 kg = 27.72 kg. That is about 28 kg.

en.text: A mineral is a natural, non-living solid with a fixed internal structure and a definite chemical make-up. Minerals are the building blocks of rocks. Most rocks are made of a few common rock-forming minerals. They form groups such as silicates, oxides, carbonates, sulfides, sulfates and chlorides.

am.text: ማዕድን የተፈጥሮ፣ ሕይወት የሌለው፣ ቋሚ ውስጣዊ መዋቅርና የተወሰነ ኬሚካላዊ ይዘት ያለው ጠጣር ነው። ማዕድናት የአለቶች መገንቢያ ናቸው። አብዛኞቹ አለቶች ከጥቂት የተለመዱ ማዕድናት የተሠሩ ናቸው። ሲሊኬቶች፣ ኦክሳይዶች፣ ካርቦኔቶች፣ ሰልፋይዶች፣ ሰልፌቶችና ክሎራይዶች በሚባሉ ቡድኖች ይከፈላሉ።

screens.title: Salt from the ground
screens.text: In the Afar region, people cut blocks of salt from the ground.
screens.ask: What do you think this rock salt is?
opts: A rock made of a mineral
screens.after: Rock salt is a mineral in the chloride group. All rocks are made of minerals.

screens.title: 1.4.2 Major minerals
paras: The crust is made of rocks, and all rocks are made of minerals.
A mineral is a natural, non-living solid. It has a fixed internal structure and a definite chemical make-up.
Minerals are the building blocks of rocks.
There are many minerals. But most rocks are made of a few common ones, called rock-forming minerals.
screens.note: Correction: the printed Table 1.2 lists quartz under oxides. Quartz is usually classed as a silicate.

screens.title: Building blocks of rocks
defs: Minerals
Natural non-living solids with a fixed structure and chemical make-up. The building blocks of rocks.

screens.title: Minerals and rocks
screens.text: How are minerals and rocks related?
opts: Minerals are only found in the core
screens.why: Minerals are the building blocks of rocks.
screens.clue: Which one is the building block?

screens.title: Mineral groups
screens.text: Match each mineral to its group.

screens.title: Where does quartz go?
screens.text: Quartz is usually classed in which mineral group?
screens.why: Quartz is a silicate. The printed book lists it under oxides, but that is an error.
screens.clue: Read the correction under the table.

screens.title: Gypsum
screens.ask: Gypsum belongs to the ___ group of minerals.
screens.clue: It is not sulfides. Look one row lower in the table.

en.text: Rocks are grouped by how they form. Igneous rocks form when magma or lava cools. Basalt cools on the surface; granite cools inside the Earth. Sedimentary rocks form in layers from settled sediments and hold fossils, coal, oil and gas. Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change existing rocks, as limestone becomes marble.

am.text: አለቶች በአፈጣጠራቸው ይመደባሉ። እሳታዊ አለቶች ማግማ ወይም ላቫ ሲቀዘቅዝ ይፈጠራሉ። ባዛልት በላይ ይቀዘቅዛል፤ ግራናይት በመሬት ውስጥ ይቀዘቅዛል። ዝቃጭ አለቶች ከተከማቹ ዝቃጮች በንብርብር ይፈጠራሉ፤ ቅሪተ አካላትን፣ ከሰል፣ ነዳጅና ጋዝ ይይዛሉ። ተለዋዋጭ አለቶች ሙቀትና ግፊት ነባር አለቶችን ሲለውጡ ይፈጠራሉ፤ ለምሳሌ ኖራ ድንጋይ እብነ በረድ ይሆናል።

screens.title: Once red-hot liquid
screens.text: Some rocks in Ethiopia were once red-hot liquid.
screens.ask: Where do you think that hot liquid came from?
screens.after: Molten rock from deep inside cooled into solid rock. That is one of three ways rocks form.

screens.title: 1. Igneous rock
paras: By how they form, rocks are grouped into three types: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.
"Igneous" comes from the Latin ignis, fire. Igneous rocks form when molten rock (magma) cools and becomes solid. This can happen on the surface or inside the Earth.
Magma that reaches the surface is called lava.
A. Extrusive igneous rocks, also called volcanic rocks, form when lava cools on the Earth's surface. Examples: basalt and obsidian.
B. Intrusive igneous rocks, also called plutonic rocks, form when magma cools and crystallises inside the Earth. Granite is the most common example.
screens.note: Focus: Magma is molten rock below the surface; it is called lava once it reaches the surface. It forms about 60–200 km deep, where temperatures are between 900°C and 1,600°C.

screens.title: Rocks from fire
defs: Igneous rock
Rock formed when magma or lava cools and hardens. From the Latin ignis, fire.
Magma
Molten rock below the Earth's surface.
Lava
Magma that has reached the Earth's surface.
Volcanic rock
Extrusive igneous rock that cooled on the surface, such as basalt.
Plutonic rock
Intrusive igneous rock that cooled deep inside the Earth, such as granite.

screens.title: Granite
screens.text: Granite cooled slowly, deep underground. What kind of rock is it?
screens.why: It formed from magma (igneous) that cooled inside the Earth (intrusive).
screens.clue: Two clues: cooled magma, and inside the Earth.

screens.title: 2. Sedimentary rock
paras: "Sedimentary" comes from the Latin sedimentum, settling.
These rocks form when sediments (mud, sand, shells) are carried by erosion. They settle in one place, mostly in rivers, seas and oceans.
They form in layers. Each layer is the sediment laid down at one time. The lower layers are usually older.
Sedimentary rocks contain fossils, which tell us about the past. They store energy resources such as coal, petroleum and natural gas.
screens.note: Correction: the printed book says the bottom layer is always the hardest and the top the softest. Older layers are usually lower, but hardness does not depend on position. The book also numbers the next section "2. Metamorphic rock"; it is the third type.

screens.title: 3. Metamorphic rock
paras: "Metamorphic" comes from the Greek meta (change) and morph (form).
Metamorphic rocks are "changed rocks". They form when existing rocks are changed by heat and pressure inside the crust.
The existing rocks can be igneous, sedimentary or even metamorphic.
Marble is an example: it forms from limestone.
screens.note: Focus: Metamorphism is the change of existing rocks into new rocks. Heat and pressure are its most important agents. Limestone → (heat and pressure) → marble.

screens.title: Settled and changed rocks
defs: Sedimentary rock
Rock formed in layers from settled sediments. Holds fossils, coal, oil and gas.
Metamorphic rock
Rock formed when heat and pressure change an existing rock. Example: marble.
Metamorphism
The change of existing rocks into new rocks by heat and pressure.

screens.title: Sort the rocks
items: Limestone changed by heat and pressure.
Formed from layers of old plants.
screens.why: Igneous: cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary: settled layers. Metamorphic: changed by heat and pressure.
screens.clue: Ask how each rock formed: cooling, settling or changing?

screens.title: Hana's rock
screens.text: On a school trip, Hana finds a rock with thin layers and tiny shells pressed inside.
screens.ask: What type of rock is it most likely?
screens.why: Layers and fossils are signs of sedimentary rock.
screens.clue: Which rock type forms in layers and holds fossils?
screens.worked: Shells are fossils. Thin layers show sediment settling over time. Both point to sedimentary rock.

screens.title: Basalt
screens.text: Basalt is an intrusive igneous rock.
screens.why: Basalt is extrusive (volcanic): it cooled on the surface. Granite is intrusive.
screens.clue: Did basalt cool on the surface or deep inside?

screens.title: Limestone changed
screens.ask: Heat and pressure change limestone into ___.
screens.why: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from limestone.
screens.clue: It is a polished stone used on floors and walls.

items.ask: 1. Igneous rocks form when ___ cools and hardens.
items.why: Igneous: magma or lava cools and hardens. Sedimentary: layers settle and harden. Metamorphic: heat and pressure change rocks.
items.clue: What is molten rock below the surface called?

items.ask: 2. Basalt is extrusive igneous rock. Granite is ___ igneous rock.

items.text: 3. Which is one of the eight major elements in the crust?
items.why: The eight are oxygen, silicon, aluminium, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium and magnesium.

items.text: 4. Feldspar, quartz, mica and olivine are silicate minerals.
items.why: Silicates: feldspar, quartz, mica, olivine. Quartz is a silicate, despite the printed table.
items.clue: Look at the first row of the mineral table.

items.text: 5. What are the most important agents of metamorphism?
items.why: Heat and pressure inside the crust change existing rocks.
items.clue: Read the Focus box about metamorphism.

test.text: The Latin word "ignis", which gives "igneous", means:
test.why: Igneous rocks form from hot molten rock.

test.text: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are found in sedimentary rocks.
test.why: Sedimentary rocks are a storehouse of energy resources.

test.text: Magma forms where temperatures are between:
test.why: Magma forms about 60–200 km deep at these temperatures.

notes.text: The printed Table 1.2 lists quartz under oxides. Quartz is usually classed as a silicate.
The printed book says the bottom sedimentary layer is always the hardest and the top the softest. Older layers are usually lower, but hardness does not depend on position.
The book numbers the metamorphic rock section "2. Metamorphic rock"; it is the third type and is shown here as 3.

The Afar rock-salt hook and the 100 kg silicon practise item are added examples. Activity 1.4 items 1–4 are open answers in the book, turned into blank/mcq/tf items using the book's answers; group discussion is skipped.
